# Song of Songs Chapter 8 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 414v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/SNG_008_page_001.jpg

---

**8:6** Set-me [simeni] as-a-seal [ka-chotam] upon your-heart [al-libbkha], as-a-seal upon your-arm [zero'ekha]; for strong [azzah] as-death [ka-mavet] [is] love [ahavah], fierce [qashah] as-Sheol [ki-she'ol] [is] jealousy [qin'ah]; its-flames [reshafeyha] [are] flames of-fire [rishpei esh], the-flame [shalhevetya] of-YAH.

**8:7** Many [rabbim] waters [mayim] cannot quench [lo yukhlu le-khabbbot] love [ha-ahavah], and-rivers [u-neharot] cannot wash-it-away [lo yishtefuha]; if a-man [ish] would-give [yitten] all the-wealth [hon] of-his-house [beito] for-love, they-would-utterly-despise [boz yavuzu] him.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**v.6 — "strong as death is love":** The theological climax of the Song. Love and death are the two great absolutes — and love is death's equal. *Shalhevetya* may contain the divine name YAH — "the very flame of the LORD." If so, this is the Song's only direct reference to God.

**v.7 — "Many waters cannot quench love":** Love is elemental, inextinguishable. No force of nature or wealth of man can overwhelm it. This may be the single most powerful statement about love in the Hebrew Bible.

*— PNEUMA*
